findings.title: The R10 firmware rule list omits the board-tied option-byte, supply, clock and USB settings that a first firmware needs and that its other rules presuppose

files: docs/FMEA_REDUNDANCY.md F-2 (line 414), F-3 (line 416), section 2.2 'Start the IWDG in software' (line 162)
evidence.option_bytes: Only BOOT_ADD0 is named ('BOOT_ADD0/relevant boot settings'). The rule 'a ROM-loader jump is allowed only before IWDG starts' (binding obligation 8; M3_R10 line 871) holds only with IWDG1_SW = software start, which FMEA section 2.2 requires but the R10 list does not. Neither list names BOR_LEV (FMEA F-3 picks level 1; DS12110 Rev 8 rev V Table 126 p217: BOR1 falling 1.95/2.00/2.06 V, rising 2.04/2.10/2.15 V; BOR3 falling 2.54/2.61/2.68 V), SWAP_BANK_OPT, RDP or IO_HSLV. These option bits exist on the H743: CMSIS stm32h743xx.h FLASH_OPTSR_IWDG1_SW, _BOR_LEV, _SWAP_BANK_OPT, _IO_HSLV, _RDP (github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis-device-h7, lines 10883-10920). DS12110 Rev 8 p250 (rev V, before Table 160): HSLV is for supplies below 2.7 V; this board runs VDD = 3V3.
evidence.supply: The board has only C19 / C20 (2.2 uF) on VCAP1 / VCAP2 (netlist) and no external VCORE, so the PWR supply configuration must be LDO (PWR_CR3 LDOEN = 1, BYPASS = 0; CMSIS PWR_CR3_LDOEN / _BYPASS / _SCUEN; community SVD reset 0x00000006). The binding fixes the clock at 200 MHz (obligation 11) but no rule names the VOS: DS12110 Rev 8 Table 122 pp214-215: VOS3 fCPU <= 200, fHCLK <= 100, fPCLK <= 50 MHz; VOS1 400 / 200 / 100 MHz; Table 123 p215 VOS0 TJ <= 105 C.
evidence.clock: Y1 is a crystal (HSEBYP = 0). 25 MHz needs DIVM so that the PLL input is 2-16 MHz and the VCO 192-960 MHz (Table 147 p239, rev V), e.g. /5, x80, /2 = 200 MHz (Calculation). FMEA V-6 / F-2 (CSSHSEON, HSE-ready timeout, HSI fallback, re-scaled safety timers) is not carried into the R10 list; on R10 HSE_IN and HSE_OUT each reach Y1 through one via, (22.00, 49.10) and (24.69, 45.50) (board, B.Cu side), so a lost HSE is a credible single fault.
evidence.usb: PA9 (OTG_FS_VBUS, DS12110 Rev 8 Table 9 p80, pin 68) is NC on R10; VBUS reaches only PC8 through R9 / R110. A device-mode USB stack must therefore not use OTG VBUS sensing (GCCFG VBDEN = 0, B-session valid override GOTGCTL BVALOEN / BVALOVAL; CMSIS names lines 24365 / 25167). The behaviour without the override is an Inference: RM0433 could not be downloaded (st.com timed out).

findings.impact: No firmware exists, so nothing fails now. A developer working from the R10 list alone could ship a hardware-started IWDG (which breaks the loader-jump rule and risks a reset loop), leave BOR at its default, run without CSS on a single-via crystal, or lose USB enumeration. Each is testable by register and option-byte readback.
findings.concrete_fix: Text only. Add a 'Bring-up configuration' bullet to docs/M3_R10.md 'Firmware' and to the binding note's obligations. Program and read back the option bytes BOOT_ADD0 = 0x0800, IWDG1_SW = software, BOR_LEV (state the level; DS12110 Table 126 p217), SWAP_BANK_OPT = 0, IO_HSLV = 0 and the RDP level. Set PWR_CR3 to LDO (never BYPASS), with the VOS matched to the 200 MHz clock (Table 122). Set HSEBYP = 0, a bounded HSE-ready wait, CSSHSEON with HSI fallback and safety-timer re-scaling (FMEA F-2), and PLL limits per Table 147. Set USB VBUS sensing off with a B-session override (PA9 NC). Label the RM0433 items as Inference until it is read.

findings.title: BOOT0's only pull-down (R5) and both VCAP capacitors (C19, C20) each hang on one via, outside SINGLE_OPEN_TAPS and unrecorded

evidence.BOOT0: U1.94 F(15.45, 46.00) -> F.Cu -> via BOOT0 (13.80, 45.60) -> B.Cu -> R5.1 B(13.00, 45.60); R5.2 B(13.00, 44.74) GND. BOOT0 has no other copper (pcbnew probe, scripts/netitems.py). DS12110 Rev 8 Table 157 p246 gives pull-up / pull-down values for I/Os but none for BOOT0, and Table 9 p86 lists BOOT0 as type B with VPP. That BOOT0 floats when the via opens is an Inference.
evidence.VCAP: VCAP1 U1.48 F(30.55, 38.00) -> via (29.25, 38.00) -> C19.1 B(28.35, 36.95); VCAP2 U1.73 F(18.00, 35.45) -> via (18.00, 37.30) -> C20.1 B(19.10, 37.30). Each net has one via and no other path. DS12110 Rev 8 Table 124 p216: CEXT 2.2 uF (+/-20 %), ESR < 100 mOhm, 'the two 2.2 uF VCAP capacitors'.
evidence.gate: tools/check_r10.py SINGLE_OPEN_TAPS (33 taps, D-R21-02 / D-R22-02) covers regulator FB / OV / EN / ILIM nodes, IC grounds and the PA4 / PA6 / 3V3 monitors; BOOT0, VCAP1 and VCAP2 are absent, and no record names these vias.
evidence.contrast: The fire and arming pull-downs are via-free: R127 / R128 (PE4) and R123 (PC1, at Q122) are on F.Cu, and R163 (PC14) sits on the gate side of the buzzer's via (20.20, 52.10).

findings.impact: BOOT0 open: at the next reset the MCU may enter the ROM loader (BOOT_ADD1 0x1FF0, Inference), so the primary recovery and roll control go silent. Fire stays safe: PC1 / PE4 stay analog with R123 / R127. On the pad, the missing telemetry shows it; after an in-flight reset, Blue Jay is the only deployment. VCAP open: the LDO keeps one 2.2 uF instead of two, below DS12110's arrangement; its stability is an Inference.
findings.concrete_fix: Now, checks only: add ('BOOT0', U1.94, R5.1), ('VCAP1', U1.48, C19.1) and ('VCAP2', U1.73, C20.1) to SINGLE_OPEN_TAPS, with exact SINGLE_OPEN_EXCEPTIONS entries and measured reasons, and list them as respin items. At the next board change, add a second via per net or move R5 to F.Cu beside U1.94.

findings.title: round22_alternates.md says FS_XL_HG 010 on the LSM6DSV80X scales wrongly by 1.6x; DS14764 and ST's driver give the same 3.904 mg/LSB as the ISM's 010, so the only difference is an 80 g clip

evidence.claim: round22_alternates.md section 2.3 (line 161): with 010, firmware would scale +/-80 g data as +/-128 g, a 1.6x error; the binding note's 001 / 010 rule is 'unsafe'. Repeated in the summary table (line 15) and the docs note (line 172).
evidence.datasheets: DS14764 Rev 1 Table 3 p12 (LSM6DSV80X): high-g sensitivity FS +/-64 g 1.952 mg/LSB, FS +/-80 g 3.904 mg/LSB; Table 138 p81: 010 = 80 g. DS15034 Rev 1 Table 3 p12 (ISM6HG256X): +/-128 g 3.904 mg/LSB; Table 150 p93: 010 = +/-128 g. DS14623 Rev 1 Table 3 p12 and Table 150 p93 (LSM6DSV320X): the same.
evidence.driver: ST lsm6dsv80x-pid lsm6dsv80x_reg.c lines 85-93: from_fs64_to_mg x1.952, from_fs80_to_mg x3.904; ism6hg256x_reg.c line 90: from_fs128_to_mg x3.904 (raw.githubusercontent.com/STMicroelectronics/*-pid/master).
evidence.also: ST's ism6hg256x_reg.h maps ISM6HG256X_256g = 0x3, but DS15034 Table 150 p93 gives 011 = Reserved and 100 = +/-256 g. The 001 / 010 rule correctly keeps firmware away from both codes.
evidence.F2: docs/REQUIREMENTS.md F2: >= +/-64 g. 001 meets it on all three parts, and so does 010 (>= +/-80 g).

findings.impact: An analysis defect, not a board defect. ORDERING section 8.1's 'LSM6DSV80XTR with FS_XL_HG 001 only' is safe but rests on a wrong reason. A firmware author reading the analysis would think the binding note's 001 / 010 rule is dangerous on the 80X. In fact one 001 / 010 driver with 1.952 / 3.904 mg/LSB serves all three parts; on the 80X, 010 clips at +/-80 g instead of +/-128 g, still above F2.
findings.concrete_fix: Text only. In round22_alternates.md section 2.3, the summary row and the docs note, replace the 1.6x claim with: 010 is 3.904 mg/LSB on all three parts (DS14764 Table 3 p12); on the 80X it clips at +/-80 g. Keep '001 only' as the conservative rule, or allow 001 / 010 with the 80 g clip noted. In the M3_R10 / binding IMU rule, add: do not use ST's ism6hg256x driver 256 g enum (0x3, reserved per DS15034 Table 150).

findings.title: Binding obligation 29 calls PB1 a TT_a pin; DS12110 gives TT_u

evidence.binding: r10_binding_note.json firmware_obligations[29]: 'open R105 puts CAM_5V on a TT_a pin through R104 10 kOhm, limit 4.0 V'.
evidence.datasheet: DS12110 Rev 8 Table 9 p70, LQFP100 pin 35 PB1: I/O structure TT_u (Table 8 p63: _u = USB option, supplied by VDD33USB); additional functions ADC12_INP5, COMP1_INM. The diagnostics sheet note already says 'TT_u 4.0 V max'.

findings.impact: Text inconsistency between two records. The 4.0 V TT limit is unchanged, so there is no electrical effect.
findings.concrete_fix: Text only: change 'TT_a' to 'TT_u' in obligation 29 (its generator in m3_firmware/assembly_binding.py or r10 binding source) and regenerate the evidence note.

fix_verification.measurement: DS15034 Table 150 p93: 000 32 / 001 64 / 010 128 / 100 256 / 011 reserved. DS14623 Table 150 p93: 011 = 256, 100 = 320. rejected_or_closed_candidates.reason: PC14 drives the AO3400A gate through 1 kOhm with R163 10k to GND: DC about 0.3 mA, transient <= 3.3 mA, against a characterised +/-3 mA (Table 159 p249). Recorded in binding 16.

rejected_or_closed_candidates.reason: SPI1 serves only U4 (netlist), so no traffic reaches it with CS high. Setting I2C_I3C_disable = 1 is optional good practice.
